title: Chronic kidney disease: evaluation and management (adult)
subject: nephrology
summary: Stage CKD by cause, GFR and albuminuria (KDIGO 2024), then slow progression with BP control, maximum tolerated ACE inhibitor or ARB, an SGLT2 inhibitor, finerenone in albuminuric type 2 diabetes and a statin, manage anaemia, acidosis and mineral bone disease, and refer on KDIGO criteria.

sections.title: Define and stage (KDIGO 2024)
items: CKD: abnormal kidney structure or function present for more than 3 months with implications for health, for example eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m2 or albuminuria (ACR 30 mg/g [3 mg/mmol] or more).
GFR categories: G1 90 or more, G2 60 to 89, G3a 45 to 59, G3b 30 to 44, G4 15 to 29, G5 below 15 mL/min/1.73 m2.
Albuminuria categories (ACR): A1 below 30 mg/g (below 3 mg/mmol), A2 30 to 300 mg/g (3 to 30 mg/mmol), A3 above 300 mg/g (above 30 mg/mmol).
Describe CKD by cause, GFR and albuminuria (CGA), for example diabetic kidney disease G3b A3. Risk of progression and cardiovascular events rises with both GFR and albuminuria category.
Common causes in India: diabetes, hypertension, chronic glomerulonephritis, obstruction and stones, analgesic or herbal medicine use, and CKD of unknown aetiology in agricultural communities.

sections.title: Evaluation
items: Creatinine-based eGFR (CKD-EPI); use combined creatinine and cystatin C eGFR when creatinine is less accurate (extremes of muscle mass, amputation, unusual diet) and the result changes decisions.
Urine ACR on an early morning sample, confirmed on repeat; dipstick and microscopy for haematuria.
Kidney ultrasound; electrolytes, bicarbonate, calcium, phosphate, PTH, ALP, 25-hydroxy vitamin D, haemoglobin, ferritin and TSAT, lipids and HbA1c.
In G3 to G5, estimate the risk of kidney failure with a validated equation such as the 4-variable KFRE.
Consider kidney biopsy when the cause is uncertain and the result would change management.

sections.title: Slow progression and cardiovascular risk
items: BP: target systolic below 120 mmHg when tolerated, using standardised office measurement; less intensive targets in frailty, falls, limited life expectancy or postural hypotension.

ACE inhibitor or ARB at the maximum tolerated dose: recommended for A3 without diabetes and for A2 to A3 with diabetes; suggested for A2 without diabetes. Never combine ACE inhibitor, ARB and direct renin inhibitor.

Check BP, creatinine and potassium 2 to 4 weeks after starting or increasing RAS blockade. Continue unless creatinine rises more than 30%; treat hyperkalaemia rather than stopping where possible; continue even when eGFR falls below 30.

SGLT2 inhibitor: recommended for type 2 diabetes with eGFR 20 or more, and for any CKD with eGFR 20 or more and ACR 200 mg/g (20 mg/mmol) or more, or heart failure; suggested for eGFR 20 to 45 with lower ACR. Continue below eGFR 20 until dialysis.

Finerenone (nonsteroidal MRA): suggested in type 2 diabetes with eGFR above 25, normal potassium and ACR above 30 mg/g (3 mg/mmol) despite maximum tolerated RAS blockade; can be added to RAS blocker plus SGLT2 inhibitor.
GLP-1 receptor agonist with proven benefit for type 2 diabetes and CKD not at glycaemic target on metformin and an SGLT2 inhibitor. Metformin: reduce the dose when eGFR is below 45 and stop below 30.

Statin or statin with ezetimibe for adults 50 or older with eGFR below 60 (not on dialysis); statin for 50 or older with G1 to G2; consider at 18 to 49 with diabetes, coronary disease, prior ischaemic stroke or high 10-year risk.
Lifestyle: protein 0.8 g/kg/day in G3 to G5 (avoid very low protein unsupervised), sodium below 2 g/day (under 5 g salt), at least 150 minutes/week moderate activity, stop tobacco, healthy weight.

sections.title: Complications
items: Anaemia (KDIGO 2026): Hb below 13 g/dL in men or 12 g/dL in women; check CBC, reticulocytes, ferritin, TSAT, B12, folate. Not on dialysis: give iron (oral or IV) if ferritin below 100 ng/mL with TSAT below 40%, or ferritin 100 to 300 ng/mL with TSAT below 25%.

Consider an ESA when Hb is 9 to 10 g/dL or lower after correcting iron and other causes; do not use an ESA to maintain Hb at 11.5 g/dL or higher. Withhold iron if ferritin is above 700 ng/mL or TSAT is 40% or more, and during active infection.
Metabolic acidosis: consider oral alkali (sodium bicarbonate) when serum bicarbonate is below 18 mmol/L, without exceeding the upper limit of normal.

CKD-MBD (KDIGO 2017): monitor calcium, phosphate, PTH and ALP from G3a; lower high phosphate towards normal with diet and binders, restrict calcium-based binders, avoid hypercalcaemia, and do not routinely use calcitriol in non-dialysis CKD.
Gout: xanthine oxidase inhibitor (allopurinol, febuxostat) for symptomatic hyperuricaemia; do not lower urate in asymptomatic hyperuricaemia to slow CKD.
Drug safety: avoid NSAIDs and nephrotoxic herbal products, dose drugs to eGFR, and give sick day guidance to pause SGLT2 inhibitor, RAS blocker, diuretics and metformin during dehydrating illness.

sections.title: Refer to nephrology (KDIGO 2024)
items: eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2, or a 5-year risk of kidney failure above 3 to 5% on a validated equation.
Sustained eGFR fall of more than 20% (more than 30% after starting RAS blocker or SGLT2 inhibitor), or AKI.
ACR above 700 mg/g (70 mg/mmol), ACR 300 mg/g (30 mg/mmol) or more with haematuria, doubling of albuminuria, red cell casts, or more than 20 red cells per high-power field unexplained.

Hypertension refractory to 4 or more drugs, persistent potassium abnormalities, acidosis, anaemia, bone disease, malnutrition, recurrent extensive stones, hereditary kidney disease, or uncertain cause.
Plan dialysis access or pre-emptive transplant when GFR is below 15 to 20 or 2-year risk of kidney failure is above 40%. Start dialysis on symptoms, signs and complications, often at GFR 5 to 10.

sections.title: Monitoring
items: eGFR and ACR at least yearly, more often (up to 4 or more times a year) in higher GFR and albuminuria risk categories.
Potassium and creatinine after any change in RAS blocker, MRA or diuretic dose.
An initial eGFR dip after starting an SGLT2 inhibitor is expected and is not a reason to stop.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Not measuring ACR, so high-risk albuminuric patients are missed.
Stopping ACE inhibitor or ARB for a creatinine rise under 30% or because eGFR fell below 30.
Stopping SGLT2 inhibitor because of the expected early eGFR dip.
Liberal calcium-based binders and active vitamin D causing hypercalcaemia and vascular calcification.
Late referral, leading to crash-start dialysis via a temporary catheter.

drugs.name: ACE inhibitor or ARB
drugs.dose: Titrate to the maximum tolerated licensed dose, for example ramipril up to 10 mg daily, telmisartan up to 80 mg daily or losartan up to 100 mg daily
drugs.notes: Check potassium and creatinine at 2 to 4 weeks; accept up to 30% creatinine rise.

drugs.name: Dapagliflozin
drugs.notes: Start at eGFR 20 or more; hold during acute illness, fasting or surgery.

drugs.name: Empagliflozin
drugs.notes: Start at eGFR 20 or more; hold during acute illness, fasting or surgery.

drugs.name: Finerenone
drugs.dose: 10 mg daily if eGFR 25 to 59; 20 mg daily if eGFR 60 or more; increase 10 mg to 20 mg after 4 weeks if potassium 4.8 mmol/L or less
drugs.notes: Product label dosing. Start only if potassium is 5.0 mmol/L or less; hold if above 5.5. Type 2 diabetes with albuminuria.

drugs.name: Metformin
drugs.dose: Reduce the dose when eGFR is below 45; stop when eGFR is below 30
drugs.notes: Pause during acute illness and around iodinated contrast if eGFR is 30 or less.
